- **TypeScript `baseUrl` ignored**: Generated TypeScript configurations [no longer use `compilerOptions.baseUrl`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#typescript-baseurl-is-ignored) to resolve Nuxt aliases
- **PostCSS plugins**: `autoprefixer` and `cssnano` are [no longer installed or configured by default](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#postcss-plugins-are-no-longer-installed-by-default)

- **Optional dependencies**: [`@vitejs/plugin-vue-jsx`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#vitejsplugin-vue-jsx-is-now-optional) and [`giget`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#giget-is-now-optional-remote-layers) are installed on demand
+- **Peer dependencies**: [`vue` and `vue-router`](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#vue-and-vue-router-are-peer-dependencies) come from your project, with `vue-router` only needed when pages are enabled
- **Removed options**: [Several experimental options](/docs/getting-started/upgrade#removed-configuration-options) are gone, because the behavior they controlled is now unconditional
If a remote layer is resolved without `giget` present, Nuxt reports which `extends` entry needs it.

+`nuxt` no longer installs its own copy of `vue` and `vue-router`. Both are peer dependencies, and Nuxt builds and runs your app with the copy your project installs. `vue-router` is optional, and only needed when pages are enabled (for example, when your app has a `pages/` directory or sets `pages: true`).
+Nuxt warns at startup if the installed `vue` or `vue-router` does not satisfy the range it supports.

+Vue keeps its rendering state per copy, so every component in an app has to use the same copy of Vue. Taking `vue` from your project means Nuxt, your app and your modules all share the copy you install.

+New Nuxt projects have listed `vue` and `vue-router` in their `package.json` for a long time, so most projects need no changes. If yours does not, Nuxt prompts you to install `vue` when it starts, and `vue-router` when pages are enabled. Nuxt requires `vue-router` v5, so if your `package.json` still lists `vue-router@^4`, upgrade it as well (see the [Vue Router migration guide](https://router.vuejs.org/guide/migration/v4-to-v5)). You can also add them yourself:

| `searchPaths` | `string[]` | `nuxt.options.modulesDir` | Additional directories to resolve packages from.                                                                                                         |

| `from`        | `string`   | `undefined` | An extra URL or path to resolve packages from, such as `import.meta.url`. Useful when your own package ships the dependency as a peer dependency.                       |

| `prompt`      | `boolean`  | `undefined` | Whether to prompt before installing. `true` always prompts, `false` never prompts (and installs automatically on StackBlitz), and leaving it unset prompts everywhere except StackBlitz. |

+| `dev`         | `boolean`  | `true`      | Whether to install the dependency as a dev dependency.                                                                                                     |
+   * Whether to install the dependency as a dev dependency.
